headline_marked: Salman Muqtadir [[hits back at Home Minister]] over studio attack
headline: Salman Muqtadir hits back at Home Minister over studio attack
summary: The content creator questioned why police didn't act immediately after his studio was looted and ransacked, challenging the government's safety promises.
details: Content creator Salman Muqtadir has criticized Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, demanding to know why police failed to act after his studio in Dhaka’s ECB Chattar was ransacked and looted.
The attack occurred at New Guinea Properties in South Manikdir around 10:30pm on Saturday. Salman’s Brownfish Studio, along with nearby structures, were targeted by attackers.

Police arrested three people following a 999 call and recovered local weapons and bullet casings. Authorities suggest the motive may be a land dispute involving a developer and a retired military officer.

Salman claims he stayed at the Cantonment Police Station until dawn on the night of the attack, but police refused to take his case. He criticized the minister for describing the incident as ‘a little vandalism’.

The content creator stated that attackers broke CCTV cameras and stole the server. He also alleged that those arrested mentioned the BNP, though he maintains he does not want to turn the incident into a political issue.
Salman challenged the Home Minister to ensure the security he promised, stating that while personal losses can be recovered, public safety is the primary concern.
caption:
Salman Muqtadir demands answers from the Home Minister after his studio was looted and ransacked. ‘Do you have any empathy?’

Content creator Salman Muqtadir has criticized Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, demanding to know why police failed to act after his studio in Dhaka’s ECB Chattar was ransacked and looted.

The attack occurred at New Guinea Properties in South Manikdir around 10:30pm on Saturday. Salman’s Brownfish Studio, along with nearby structures, were targeted by attackers.

Police arrested three people following a 999 call and recovered local weapons and bullet casings. Authorities suggest the motive may be a land dispute involving a developer and a retired military officer.

Salman claims he stayed at the Cantonment Police Station until dawn on the night of the attack, but police refused to take his case. He criticized the minister for describing the incident as ‘a little vandalism’.

The content creator stated that attackers broke CCTV cameras and stole the server. He also alleged that those arrested mentioned the BNP, though he maintains he does not want to turn the incident into a political issue.

Salman challenged the Home Minister to ensure the security he promised, stating that while personal losses can be recovered, public safety is the primary concern.

Source: bdnews24.com, Jamuna TV, The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune

headline: 9 die in 24 hours as measles death toll reaches 1,096 in Bangladesh
summary: The DGHS reports 1,228 new suspected cases and 113 confirmed infections in a single day, highlighting a severe outbreak.
details: Nine patients died with measles-like symptoms within 24 hours, bringing the total number of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 1,096 this year.
According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), all nine of the latest fatalities are classified as suspected deaths, with no confirmed deaths reported in the last 24 hours.
The total number of suspected measles deaths has now reached 995, while laboratory-confirmed deaths stand at 101.
In the last 24 hours alone, 1,228 new suspected cases and 113 new confirmed infections were recorded nationwide.
The cumulative number of suspected cases has reached 188,041, while total laboratory-confirmed infections stand at 21,212.
Since March 15, 166,310 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 159,519 have recovered.
The DGHS continues to monitor the situation as the outbreak spreads across the country.
caption:
1,096 deaths and over 188,000 suspected cases. Bangladesh is facing a severe measles outbreak.

Nine patients died with measles-like symptoms within 24 hours, bringing the total number of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 1,096 this year.

According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), all nine of the latest fatalities are classified as suspected deaths, with no confirmed deaths reported in the last 24 hours.

The total number of suspected measles deaths has now reached 995, while laboratory-confirmed deaths stand at 101.

In the last 24 hours alone, 1,228 new suspected cases and 113 new confirmed infections were recorded nationwide.

The cumulative number of suspected cases has reached 188,041, while total laboratory-confirmed infections stand at 21,212.

Since March 15, 166,310 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 159,519 have recovered.

The DGHS continues to monitor the situation as the outbreak spreads across the country.
